_comment: Campaign 02: does `Lose` DO anything at level-load time, or is it merely
dispatched? Campaign 01 falsified its own prediction P3 -- a console
command placed after `Lose` still ran, 3/3 -- and then the artefacts
refused to say what that meant: lose_before.txt and lose_after.txt came
back BYTE-IDENTICAL in all three replicates, and the arm's decision time
was indistinguishable from baseline.
That is the 2026-07-31 shape exactly. Two explanations, one observation:
CLAIM  the console queue survives a mission-outcome transition.
RIVAL  `Lose` was dispatched and did nothing observable here -- gated by
the game-state value at 0x008a9ac0 that PROBE-CONSOLE-2026-08-02
section 7.1 shows gates `Win` and `Map`, or deferred to a tick
that never came. Nothing survived anything.
Both predict every single thing campaign 01 measured. Promoting the claim
on that evidence is the error the refuter exists to catch.
THE DISCRIMINATOR. If `Lose` is indistinguishable from a command that does
not exist, the rival stands. So one arm issues ZZNOTACOMMAND in the exact
position `Lose` occupied. Nothing in the engine can act on it -- it is not
in the 33-entry command table -- so it is a floor for 'did nothing'.
`Win` is included because section 7.1 says the same state value gates it,
and a claim about one is worth little without the other.
PREDICTIONS, REGISTERED IN ADVANCE. This commit is the timestamp and it
precedes the first launch.
Q1  All three of losecmd, wincmd and noopcmd report PASS 3/3: the command
after the one under test always runs.
FALSIFIED BY: any of them failing to produce its _after file.
Q2  THE DISCRIMINATOR. losecmd is distinguishable from noopcmd on at least
one of: before/after MemStats byte-equality, decision-time median
beyond the within-arm spread, or exit-code distribution.
EXPECTED UNDER THE CLAIM: losecmd differs from noopcmd somewhere.
EXPECTED UNDER THE RIVAL: losecmd and noopcmd are indistinguishable on
every one of the three, because a dispatched-but-inert command and a
command that does not exist leave the same trace -- none.
FALSIFIED BY: no measurable difference. That kills the claim, and it is
the outcome the reasoning above actually predicts.
Q3  before/after MemStats stay byte-identical in every arm including
noopcmd, because all autoexec lines are dispatched in one burst during
level load, before the simulation ticks.
FALSIFIED BY: any arm whose before and after differ. That would make
MemStats a usable within-burst state probe, which would be a better
instrument than anything currently available without elevation.
SCOPE. Nothing here measures life, shields, the augment chain or the death
path. Level 100 only. No coverage: TTD needs elevation, this does not use
it, and no statement about which functions executed is possible.
